correctness.rationale: The exact projected-ReLU arc integral has three cases. Along any nested-circle interpolation the projected center moves at speed at most the radius growth; the worst directional derivative reduces to 2r(1+cos alpha)(2 tan(alpha/2)-alpha)>=0. Convex nonnegative scalar functions are positive sums/integrals of hinges and a nonnegative constant on the compact relevant interval. Rotational averaging yields radial powers p>=1; angular directions perpendicular to the center give strictness. A direct radial-tail arc computation gives the negative square-root tangency correction and smoothing by dominated convergence. All boundaries and quantifiers are covered. The 2703 program diagnostics are not relied on for universality.

value.rationale: The geometry of disk inclusion rescues a broad nonconstant weighted perimeter class from the general rigidity obstruction. The theorem simultaneously treats all scalar convex ridges and all real radial powers p>=1, without the weight-origin containment hypothesis, and distinguishes them sharply from general smooth increasing radial weights by a quantitative square-root failure at tangency. This is a meaningful structural boundary for a natural variational invariant, not an arbitrary finite computation.
